plan.summary: Fixes a race in `count`: it no longer checks `dir.exists()` before reading. A missing directory is now handled by `read_dir` returning `NotFound`, which yields `(0, 0)`. The PR also removes the explicit `drop(guard)` telemetry flush from `main`.
plan.riskRationale: The count change is small and removes a check-then-read race. The `main.rs` change removes an explicit flush before `std::process::exit`. `exit` does not run destructors, so telemetry may be lost. The PR description does not mention this.
plan.storyArc: The stated goal is a race-free file count. The `count` change does that by relying on the read error. The `main` change is unrelated to that goal and may change telemetry behavior at exit, so it gets its own review.

topics.title: Handle a missing directory in the read, not by a prior check
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `count` now treat a missing directory, and why does that remove the race? Verify that other errors still propagate and that `NotFound` from `read_dir` returns `(0, 0)` as the old check did.

topics.title: Telemetry guard no longer dropped before exit
topics.narrativeBrief: What happens to the telemetry flush when `drop(guard)` is removed and `std::process::exit` is called? Verify that `exit` skips destructors and that the guard has no other flush path. Note that the PR description does not explain this change.
